solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Switches bottle, needing no answer in case of shingles

indicators.note: what you need no more of can be left out, so 'answer' comes away from 'bottle'
the bottle word sits in the shingles letters, enclosed between them
a case is the outside that holds something, so only the outer letters of 'shingles' count

blocks.note: the case of a word is its outside pair of letters
bottle is nerve or pluck; drop the A that abbreviates answer

explanation.surface: Someone treating shingles swaps one medicine bottle for another.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, so the medicine-cabinet reading is a blind; A for answer is the standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Scourges and switches are both whips, thin flexible rods once used for flogging people.

clue.text: B-lister’s harangue at person performing priestly duties?

blocks.note: a B-list name is a minor celebrity, a celeb
to harangue is to rant

explanation.surface: A minor celebrity loses their temper at a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: a celebrant is whoever leads the rite, not always a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrant is the officiant who conducts a religious ceremony such as Mass or Communion.

clue.text: Express’s topless spread

indicators.note: without a top means the head of 'spread' is removed, which in a down entry is its first letter

blocks.note: a spread on toast is BUTTER; without its top letter the B goes

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about a racy photo feature in the Daily Express.
explanation.walkthrough: Spread reads as a newspaper page layout, but it is the butter; in a down answer the top is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to say it aloud, voicing or stating it in words.

clue.text: Duck slime? Smoother!

blocks.note: goo is sticky slime
a sander smooths wood

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from a slimy duck and wants something smoother.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck looks like a verb telling you to dodge the slime; it is the bird. The goosander is a large diving duck of northern rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander is a species of sawbill waterfowl, called common merganser in North America.

clue.text: Help in mass, for example

blocks.note: assistance offered, as when a shop is at your disposal
Mass is one kind of church rite

explanation.surface: Someone gets help while at Mass, or in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass is printed lower case, so it passes for a crowd or a physics quantity until you read it as the church rite.
explanation.definitionFit: Service means assistance given, and also a formal act of religious worship like the Eucharist.

clue.text: Son has no trousers

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
someone who has none of a thing lacks it

explanation.surface: A boy turns up without any trousers on.
explanation.walkthrough: The sentence reads as complete, but 'has no' is the middle piece and 'trousers' the noun answering it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slacks are casual trousers, a loose-fitting type of leg garment.

clue.text: Reject incentive, and without cover

indicators.note: uncovered means its outside wrapping is gone, so only what lies inside 'and' is kept

blocks.note: a spur is a stimulus or incentive
strip the outer letters from 'and' and only its middle remains

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a bonus, and one offered without any insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a joining word, but it is the fodder whose covering letters come off.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to refuse or turn away with contempt, a stronger kind of rejection.

clue.text: Amazed when lorry gets both of us on board

indicators.note: passengers on board are inside the vehicle, so 'both of us' ends up inside 'when'
the lorry gets added on, joining the pieces one after another

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
the pronoun for you and me together
a lorry is the British word for a truck

explanation.surface: Two hitchhikers are astonished when a lorry stops and lets them aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The pronoun sits aboard the conjunction, and the vehicle follows; 'lorry' is British for a large goods vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with wonder, so overwhelmed with astonishment or reverence.

clue.text: Equipment best uncovered for so-called planes

indicators.note: with its covering stripped off, 'best' keeps only its inner letters

blocks.note: kit is gear or equipment
with its outer letters taken off, only the middle two of 'best' remain

explanation.surface: An aviation catalogue lists its best gear for aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' warns that the definition is slang: kite was old RAF slang for an aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Kite is informal wartime airmen's slang for an aircraft, hence the hedge in the clue.

clue.text: Student coming in almost last, drunk

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word for 'last' loses its final letter
the student comes into the other word, entering it and ending up enclosed

blocks.note: last place is the bottom, cut short by its final letter
L for learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student staggers home near the back of the field, having had too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Last reads as a race position, and it is: last place is the bottom of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for very drunk, completely intoxicated.

clue.text: Rent during course is a risky game

indicators.note: one thing happening during another lies within its span, so 'rent' goes inside 'course'

blocks.note: a route is a course taken
to rent out a flat is to let it

explanation.surface: Renting somewhere while on a course is a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: One piece goes inside another, as 'during' puts it within the time of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino wheel betting game, a byword for taking dangerous chances.

clue.text: Planning a near orbit must be an anomaly

indicators.note: planning is arranging things anew, so the letters of 'a near orbit' get rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A space agency plotting a low orbit concludes something is amiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planning' rearranges its fodder the way a planner arranges things; the space surface fits, since aberration is also an astronomical term.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a departure from what is normal or expected, an irregularity.

clue.text: Put back time trial

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so 'put' is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to put a thing down is to set it
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Organisers postpone a time trial, the cycling race against the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' reads as postponed, but 'put' is the word and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A test and a trial are both an examination of how something performs.

clue.text: Off colour initially in fixing drain

indicators.note: fixing a thing means reworking it, so the letters of 'drain' are rearranged
initially points to the first letter, here of 'colour' only
the colour letter goes in the reworked drain, enclosed by it

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the opening letter of colour

explanation.surface: A plumber feels unwell while fixing a blocked drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off colour' is a ready-made phrase for poorly, but the words split: 'Off' is the definition and 'colour' gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off is rancid, with the stale sour smell of spoiled fat.

clue.text: Gamble supporting company fight showing lack of courage

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so 'gamble' goes below 'company fight'

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a war is a fight between nations
to dice is to gamble

explanation.surface: A firm that bets rather than fights shows it lacks nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath, so the first word of the clue comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardice is the absence of bravery, being too fearful to face danger.

clue.text: Illustrates old stamps

blocks.note: an ex-something is a former or old one
to stamp heavily is to pound

explanation.surface: An illustrator decorates antique postage stamps.
explanation.walkthrough: Stamps looks like a noun for philatelists and is a verb; 'Illustrates' is likewise a verb meaning explains.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out and explain in detail, making a point clear by example.

clue.text: Customs may see a bit of drama cutting costs

indicators.note: cutting into something splits it open, so 'a bit of drama' goes into the middle of 'costs'

blocks.note: costs are what things are priced at
an act is one section of a play

explanation.surface: Customs officers make a scene while cutting costs.
explanation.walkthrough: Customs suggests the border service, but it means habits; 'cutting' puts one piece into the middle of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs and practices are both habitual ways of doing things within a group.

clue.text: Mad English composer touring carnival venue

indicators.note: touring a place means going all round it, so the composer wraps round the carnival city

blocks.note: Frederick Delius, English composer
Rio de Janeiro hosts the famous carnival

explanation.surface: A frenzied English composer goes on tour to a carnival city.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer goes round the city, as someone touring a place goes all round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirious means wildly excited or temporarily deranged, out of one's senses.

clue.text: Cooks must cross a road for high-flying workers

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it from side to side, so 'cooks' straddles 'a road'

blocks.note: to stew is to cook slowly
A plus RD, the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Chefs have to cross a street to reach their high-powered office jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: High-flying sounds like ambitious executives; here it is literal, cabin crew who work in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards serve passengers aboard aircraft, so their work happens at altitude.

clue.text: Person who looks small – tinker?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
to tinker idly is to potter about

explanation.surface: Someone who seems little is taken for a wandering tinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Looks small reads as appearance, but 'looks' closes the definition and 'small' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotter watches out for things, like a trainspotter or aircraft observer.

clue.text: Talk a little about a remedy for acid

indicators.note: the answer is found about, that is around and within, the words 'Talk a little'

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words, losing only the ends

explanation.surface: A doctor chats briefly about a cure for indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the second letter of 'Talk' to the middle of 'little'; 'a little' is doing double duty as fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An alkali neutralises acids chemically, which is how antacid tablets settle a stomach.

clue.text: Lead shot originally used with pitch

indicators.note: originally points at the origin of 'shot', its very first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of shot
pitch is black tar

explanation.surface: Lead pellets were first fired together with a sticky black coating.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead suggests the metal alongside shot and pitch; it is the leading role in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The star of a film or play takes the leading part, the principal role.

clue.text: Subject of note crossing border

indicators.note: the note stretches across the border, its two letters landing on either side

blocks.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a hem is the border of cloth

explanation.surface: A letter carried across a frontier is the matter under discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: Note suggests a written message, but it is a musical note; the note spans the border as it crosses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme is the subject or topic of a piece of writing or talk.

clue.text: Such vehicles bear the marks of battle

blocks.note: to sport something is to bear or wear it visibly
wounds leave scars

explanation.surface: Some cars come out of combat visibly dented and damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such' points back at the whole sentence: the definition only makes sense once the wordplay has built the vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports cars are fast low two-seater motors, the kind described by the wordplay.

clue.text: What’s left of building after the end of this inferno?

indicators.note: the end means the final letter, so only the last of 'this' is taken
the inferno word comes after the single letter, following it in order

blocks.note: the final letter of this
an inferno is hell

explanation.surface: Firefighters ask what remains of a house once the blaze burns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the end letter first, as it follows the building in the sentence but leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell is the gutted outer walls of a building with the interior destroyed.

clue.text: Antique copper ring in Orkney, originally

indicators.note: originally takes the origin of each of 'ring in Orkney', their first letters

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the opening letters of those three words

explanation.surface: An old copper ring turns up on the Scottish islands of Orkney.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring invites the letter O, but 'originally' reaches back over three words; Orkney is an island group off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a rare or unusual collectable object, often an old ornament.

clue.text: Architectural feature may be obstacle having ignored first two letters

indicators.note: ignoring the opening pair means dropping them from the word for 'obstacle'

blocks.clueFragment: obstacle having ignored first two letters
blocks.note: an obstacle is an impediment; lose its opening pair

explanation.surface: A building's ornament might get in the way if you skip the first letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The instruction is spelt out plainly: the I and M at the start go.
explanation.definitionFit: A pediment is the triangular gable above a classical portico, as on Greek temples.

clue.text: Taxi working to load right element

indicators.note: a taxi that loads something takes it inside, so 'right' goes into 'taxi'

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
R is the abbreviation for right
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A cab driver on shift loads the correct item.
explanation.walkthrough: The taxi loads the letter for right, and the word for working follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon is chemical element number six, the basis of organic chemistry.

clue.text: Withdraw toll applied to soldiers

indicators.note: applied to means stuck onto, so 'toll' is attached after 'soldiers'

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
bells toll or peal

explanation.surface: A road charge imposed on troops gets cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Toll reads as a fee, but it is the sound of a bell; the Royal Engineers are a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or cancel it officially.

clue.text: Reaction of revolutionary press on right of choice

indicators.note: a revolution turns everything over, so 'press on' and the extra letter are jumbled
the right of a word is its right-hand end, so only the final letter of 'choice'

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the rightmost letter of choice

explanation.surface: Radical newspapers comment on the right to choose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary press' reads as a radical newspaper, but the adjective is the anagram signal; 'right of' means the letter at the right-hand end.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is an answer or reply, the way someone reacts to something.
